meta.title: Meteor-M LRPT receive chain: QPSK, Viterbi, sync and derandomising
meta.tools: NumPy/SciPy: RRC pulse shaping, Costas carrier loop, Gardner timing, soft Viterbi (k=7, r=½), CCSDS ASM search
meta.summary: Build the digital chain that turns a Meteor-M LRPT QPSK signal into CCSDS frames: carrier and symbol recovery, the k = 7 rate-½ convolutional decoder, the 0x1ACFFC1D sync marker and the CCSDS pseudo-random derandomiser — tested end-to-end on a standards-conformant synthetic signal with Doppler-like frequency offset and noise.
meta.problem: LRPT is the digital successor of APT: 72 ksym/s QPSK with forward error correction. What does each stage of the receiver contribute, and how much coding gain does the Viterbi decoder buy?
meta.theory:
Rate-½, K = 7 convolutional code (polynomials 171/133 octal) with soft Viterbi decoding has free distance 10 and ≈ 5 dB
coding gain at BER 10⁻⁵ over uncoded QPSK. Uncoded QPSK: $BER=Q(\sqrt{2E_b/N_0})$. Frames start with the 32-bit
attached sync marker 0x1ACFFC1D; data are XOR-ed with the CCSDS PN sequence $h(x)=x^8+x^7+x^5+x^3+1$ (period 255),
so derandomising a frame twice returns it unchanged.
meta.method:
Transmitter: 40 random 1020-byte frames → CCSDS randomiser → ASM prepended → conv. encoder → QPSK → RRC (α = 0.6, 8 samples/symbol)
→ +1.2 kHz carrier offset at 72 ksym/s, random phase → AWGN. Receiver: Costas loop, Gardner timing recovery, RRC
matched filter, soft Viterbi, ASM correlation search (with phase-ambiguity resolution), derandomise. BER measured
vs E_b/N₀ for coded and uncoded paths.
meta.data: Synthetic signal built to the CCSDS/Meteor-M LRPT specifications (real Meteor IQ recordings are not archived by SatNOGS).

rows.quantity: Coding gain at BER 10⁻⁴ (Eb/N0 uncoded − coded)
rows.note: textbook ≈5 dB at 10⁻⁵, a bit less at 10⁻⁴

rows.quantity: Frames recovered after carrier lock (ASM found)
